drafted_from: tool:hear-for-a-device row in tools/listen-for-a-while/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json, hearForADevice and hearPieces in read-data/listen-for-a-while.mjs, and the test in test/listen-for-a-while.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Hear the recording /Recordings/phone-piece.m4a that my Phone made at 2026-10-31T12:00:00Z, call the listening p1, and use the Whisper model I keep at ~/models/ggml-base.bin." It runs tool:hear-for-a-device and tells you the turns it heard.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it reads the one recording through the files door and answers the heard turns; it writes no row and no file.
instructions: 1. Put the recording in your files (the door finds it by name) and have a ggml Whisper model file and the whisper-cli and ffmpeg programs on the computer that will hear it; enrol the voices you want named with tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face first.

2. Say "Hear the recording <file> that my <device> made at <time>" with the model path; your AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run and tool tool:hear-for-a-device (file, device and model_path are required; at, listening, voice_prints, voice_session, recording_rules, recording_facts, listening_switch and transcriber are optional).

3. Read the answer: pieces and turns count what was heard, and `heard` holds one heard row per turn; let_go and blocked say when a recording rule or a pause let the piece go unheard; leaves and stays list what leaves this computer and what stays. The tool keeps nothing: keep `heard` where you keep such things.
4. Use the same listening name and hand back the answer's `voice_session` to continue an earlier listening so unknown voices keep their numbers (voice-1 stays voice-1).

worked_examples.title: A phone's recording becomes one heard row in the answer
worked_examples.ask: Hear the recording my Phone made at noon on 31 October and tell me who said what.
worked_examples.given: From tools/listen-for-a-while/test/listen-for-a-while.test.mjs (the test replaces hearing and naming with stand-ins): the door holds /Recordings/phone-piece.m4a, the hearing step returns one stretch from 1 s to 2 s with the text "from the phone", and the naming step labels it Someone (voice-1).
worked_examples.hands_back: The answer's `heard` holds one heard row with id heard:p1:1793448001000 (the start time plus 1 s) whose device is Phone and text is "from the phone"; the answer says listening "p1", pieces 1, turns 1, left_out 0, let_go 0, blocked null, paused null, heard_until "2026-10-31T12:00:00.000Z", with the leaves and stays lists. Nothing is written: the copy read for hearing is deleted, and the recording in your files is left where it is. Without device the run refuses with "Say which device recorded this"; without file with "Give `file`".
